Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal at AsterCloud asked us to confirm a couple of public-facing bullets in the hosted API and Console copy before we sign the SOW. High level asks:

1) We need unambiguous language on subprocessors — can you confirm the list that will be published and how often it updates?
2) For data transfers, is the phrase "we may transfer" sufficient or do you use SCCs/adequacy language in the DPA?
3) They want a short snippet we can put in our vendor inventory that explains retention and whether Redwood uses any human reviewers for hosted API content.

I've attached AsterCloud's vendor intake template and a draft phrasing we think would work — would appreciate a short set of public copy options (one-sentence and two-sentence) and a yes/no on SCCs.

Best,

Kimberly —

High level from legal: we will include Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) in the DPA for transfers out of the EEA; our current DPA references SCCs and we keep an appendix with transfer mechanisms. So answer to AsterCloud's SCC question is: yes, we rely on SCCs and/or adequacy decisions as applicable.

Subprocessor publication: we publish an up-to-date list on the public page and a timestamped audit log in our Console (we publish changes monthly and after any material onboarding). We should avoid wording that guarantees no changes; propose "This list is updated monthly and may be updated between publications to reflect business changes."

Human review: our Hosted API does not use human reviewers for customer prompts unless the customer opts into a managed review program or there is a security incident that requires triage. We must be explicit — do NOT use phrasing like "no human ever".

Proposed short legal-safe snippets (pick whichever fits product tone):
- One-line: "Redwood processes requests using our hosted inference service; subprocessors and transfer mechanisms (e.g., SCCs) are documented in our DPA and on the subprocessors page."
- Two-line: "Redwood processes customer requests to operate the Hosted API and Console. We publish an up-to-date list of subprocessors and rely on SCCs and other lawful transfer mechanisms for cross-border transfers; human reviewers are used only with explicit customer consent or during security triage."

I've attached the DPA redline for reference (DPA_Greenwave_Redline_20260301.pdf).

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Quick product notes —

Thanks Priya, that's very helpful. A couple of practical constraints and suggested final copy for the docs/Console UI: we want the public-facing copy to be short and avoid legal jargon while remaining accurate. Also, in the Console we'll have a small info panel, so propose: 

- Tooltip (one-line): "We publish our subprocessors and transfer mechanisms in the DPA and Console; see details for region-specific controls."
- Expanded modal (two-line + link): "Redwood's Hosted API processes customer requests and stores transient request metadata to support caching/optimization. Subprocessors and transfer mechanisms (including SCCs) are listed in the DPA and on the subprocessors page; human review occurs only with customer consent or to investigate incidents. [Learn more]"

Notes: we cannot say "stores request content indefinitely" — retention varies by customer configuration and retention settings in the Console. Use the phrase "retention depends on customer configuration; see DPA and settings."

Marcus: confirm we can surface the last-updated timestamp in the Console for subprocessors and add the 'last published' string. If monthly cadence is hard, we should say "updated monthly or as needed."

—Mike

Helen / AsterCloud legal —

Thanks for raising these questions. Below is the consolidated response and suggested public copy you can use in your vendor inventory:

1) Subprocessors: We publish an up-to-date subprocessors list at https://redwood.ai/subprocessors and show a "last published" timestamp in the Console. The list is updated monthly and may be updated between publications to reflect business changes.

2) Transfers: Our DPA incorporates Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for transfers out of the EEA; we also rely on adequacy decisions when applicable. The DPA appendix documents the mechanisms.

3) Human review and retention: For Hosted API customers, human reviewers are not used for customer prompts by default. Human review occurs only with explicit customer consent (e.g., managed review program) or when necessary to investigate abuse or security incidents. Retention of request content depends on customer-configured retention settings; the DPA and Console settings page describe options.

Suggested vendor inventory snippet (one sentence):
"Redwood Inference processes requests for the Hosted API; subprocessors and transfer mechanisms (including SCCs) are published in the DPA and on the subprocessors page; human review occurs only with customer consent or for incident triage."

I've attached the redlined DPA and a proposed privacy snippet for your vendor inventory. If that works, we'll prepare an updated public page and Console copy next week and share a screenshot.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Head of Customer Contracts, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
